title: Separate a molecular attachment from a retained old-new bridge
statement: For integer v>=1 independent identical arms, each yields a retained old graft with probability u*theta, retained new graft u*(1-theta), or no retained graft1-u. Pcross=1-(1-u*theta)^v-(1-u*(1-theta))^v+(1-u)^v. At fixed total u in[0,1], theta=1/2 maximizes Pcross; splitting unchanged opportunities into old/new stages cannot exceed that balanced model.

requires: Independent identical arms with exclusive old/new/none retained outcomes and actual molecular contact; u=q*eta only when the declared graft/retention decomposition is valid.
A Poisson weaker-end load count additionally needs independently justified endpoint populations and actual mechanical assumptions.
provides: For integer v>=1 independent identical arms, each yields a retained old graft with probability u*theta, retained new graft u*(1-theta), or no retained graft1-u. Pcross=1-(1-u*theta)^v-(1-u*(1-theta))^v+(1-u)^v. At fixed total u in[0,1], theta=1/2 maximizes Pcross; splitting unchanged opportunities into old/new stages cannot exceed that balanced model.
assumptions: Balanced staging comparison freezes total per-arm retained success; allosteric changes, selective loops or a persistent preanchor change the interface.
No actual u,theta,eta or mechanically sustained junction force is acquired from biochemical attachment counts.
costs: Count every arm, failed graft and donor-cleavage loss. Actual load transfer, creep, force sharing, wet retention and enzyme/reactant supply remain separate costs/evidence.
contract.units: u,theta,q,eta and Pcross are probabilities; v and capped junction counts are dimensionless. Force is not obtained without a supplied mechanical law.
contract.obstruction: Acquire a genuinely two-sided, mechanically retained wet connection rather than equating molecular grafts with structural repair.

body: Exclude the no-old and no-new events and add back no-graft. The two excluded powers have a convex sum in theta, so their minimum is symmetric. One arm cannot form this two-sided bridge, and a chemical graft lacking retention in its donor network does not supply a useful end. If separate old/new fibre ends have iid Poisson(mu) useful-junction counts, for K>=0 and mu>=0 the capped weaker-end expected count is sum_{j=1}^floorK Pr[Pois(mu)>=j]^2+(K-floorK)*Pr[Pois(mu)>=floorK+1]^2. This is a count identity under a separate independence/cap model, not a measured force or fracture-energy law.

review.scope: Completed source-exposed author reconstruction of old/new inclusion-exclusion and the balanced fixed-budget maximum; Poisson thinning conditional on a common clock and Jensen comparison; four-arm small-time quadratic expansion and Laplace N^-1/2 tail; guaranteed positive catalytic-time bound; and the independent exponential contact-race ceiling. The declared capped weaker-end Poisson count is a conditional tail-sum identity, not an accepted constitutive law. Full scientific response and original code were statically read; no code import, quadrature, optimization or Monte Carlo was executed. Primary biochemical/mechanical claims and actual device or regenerative operation are not newly validated.
